(a) In General.—Section 2 of Public Law 87–788 (commonly known as the “McIntire-Stennis Cooperative Forestry Act”) (16 U.S.C. 582a–1) is amended by inserting “and 1890 Institutions (as defined in section 2 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7601)),” before “and (b)”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) takes effect on October 1, 2008.

fable.w: The section only amends the McIntire-Stennis Cooperative Forestry Act to add 1890 Institutions to the entities eligible for forestry research assistance, and sets an effective date. The tempting reading is that "Cooperative" in the Act's name, or the mention of outside institutions, signals coordination with non-federal parties, but that is just a proper noun and an eligibility expansion for funding. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
fable.s: is amended by inserting “and 1890 Institutions (as defined in section 2 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7601)),” before “and (b)”.

opus.w: The amendment only adds 1890 Institutions to the list of schools that can receive forestry research funding under the McIntire-Stennis Act. That is about who can get a benefit or grant, which the definition excludes. The word "Cooperative" in the Act's name is boilerplate. The section does not create any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: is amended by inserting “and 1890 Institutions (as defined in section 2 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7601)),” before “and (b)”
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the amended statute is the McIntire-Stennis *Cooperative* Forestry Act, and section 2 covers the Secretary working with outside institutions such as land-grant colleges. That reading fails. This amendment only adds 1890 Institutions to the list of schools that can get forestry research funding. Being eligible for a grant is not participation. The section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue before a federal decision. "Cooperative" here is just part of the Act's name.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to include 1890 Institutions in the list of eligible entities for a forestry program. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by these institutions or any other outside parties in the decision-making process. It is a definition of eligibility, not a participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: Section 2 of Public Law 87–788 (commonly known as the “McIntire-Stennis Cooperative Forestry Act”) (16 U.S.C. 582a–1) is amended by inserting “and 1890 Institutions (as defined in section 2 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7601)),” before “and (b)”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that adding "1890 Institutions" to the list of eligible entities implies a form of participation or consultation with these institutions. However, the text merely amends the list of eligible recipients for a program; it does not establish a process for these institutions to consult with the government, provide input on decisions, or participate in an advisory capacity. It is a statutory amendment defining eligibility, not a procedural requirement for public participation.
